# Hosea 3: research notes

**Coverage:** I found nothing on this chapter from netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org, Orthodox sites, Lutheran or Pentecostal denominational sites, or prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teachers, so those are left out. The only Catholic source is Haydock (1849) on studylight.org. The tradition labels below (Baptist, Methodist and so on) are my general descriptions of the writers, not something the pages state.

## v. 1

**Traditional reading**
- **God's love for unfaithful people:** Guzik says Hosea is told to love a wife who is committing adultery right now, not in the past. He also says God's love for us should make us more loving and forgiving toward others. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
- **Love as a choice:** Guzik argues that love is largely a matter of the will, not romantic capture. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
- **"Again":** Barnes says Hosea loved her before she fell and was to keep loving her during her fall, to rescue her from it. God was watching over Israel and they, all the while, were looking to other gods. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm
- **"Loved by another":** Ellicott reads it this way and thinks Gomer may now be another man's slave-concubine, possibly in poverty. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm
- **Raisin cakes:** Ellicott calls them sacrificial cakes used in idol worship (compare Jeremiah 7:18). Barnes says the wine stands for the excess of idolatry, and the cakes for any pleasure preferred to God. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm
- **Wider application:** Matthew Henry sees here God's gracious dealings with fallen mankind and the covenant of grace. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm
- **The Hebrew word:** The Bible Hub summary says the word for love (*ahav*) means deep, unconditional, covenant love. https://biblehub.com/hosea/3.htm

**Where traditions differ**
- **Divorce:** Guzik says the verse shows that Scripture permits divorce for adultery but does not command it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
- **Who is the woman?**
  - *Gomer:* Barnes, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown and the Pulpit homiletics. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/hosea/3.htm
  - *A different woman:* Benson (a Methodist) cites Jerome and Cyril of Alexandria for this. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-1.htm
  - *An imagined figure in a parable:* Gill (a Baptist) says she is not Gomer but some other feigned person. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/3.htm
- **"Her friend":** Wesley (Methodist) takes this to mean her husband. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/

**Catholic**
- Haydock says the woman stands for penitent Israel, yet not quite reconciled. Hosea gives his word but does not marry her. Grace is still offered to sinners, whom God never hates as persons. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/hosea-3.html

## v. 2

**Traditional reading**
- **The price:** The Pulpit Commentary says the silver plus the barley came to about 30 shekels, the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32). Barley was the offering for a woman suspected of adultery (Numbers 5). The small sum points to the woman's low and distressed condition. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/3.htm
- **Wesley:** 15 shekels was half a slave's value, and barley was the poorest food. Together they show Israel's poverty and ingratitude, and God's generosity. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/
- **Gill:** The price stands for Israel's captive, servile, mean, and abject state until their conversion to Christ. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/3.htm
- **Pulpit homiletics:** The scene pictures what sin does to people in general, not only to Israel. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/hosea/3.htm

**Where interpreters differ: who was paid, and why?**
- The Pulpit Commentary lists three options: a bride-price paid to her parents, a marriage gift paid to her, or a payment to a husband she had betrayed. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/3.htm
- Guzik thinks Hosea bought her out of prostitution, going the "extra mile." He notes that Boice thinks she was sold as a slave. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
- An application quoted on Precept Austin: God buys us out of sin's bondage through the death of Christ. https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-3-commentary

## v. 3

**Traditional reading**
- **A time of waiting:** The Pulpit Commentary says Hosea keeps her apart from all men, including himself. She waits in patient hope of his favour. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/3.htm
- **Clarke:** Hosea did not take her home. He gave her the money and barley to live on so she would not be tempted back into unfaithfulness. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/hosea-3.html
- **Wesley:** She would wait unmarried until he took her as his wife. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/

**Where interpreters differ: "and I will do the same for you"**
- Precept Austin notes there is no verb in the Hebrew. Which verb you supply is the interpretive crux of the verse. https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-3-commentary
- **Hosea also abstains from her:** Pulpit Commentary, Coffman and Keil & Delitzsch. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/3.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/hosea-3.html
- **Hosea waits for her and takes no other wife:** Gill. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/3-3.html
- **Living together is the goal:** Guzik reads "stay with me" as restored relationship. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/

**Catholic**
- Haydock (citing Calmet) says Hosea did not appear to marry her; it signified that the people must wait for God in captivity. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/hosea-3.html

## v. 4

**Traditional reading**
- **Three losses (Guzik):** no political leadership, no spiritual service, no supernatural guidance. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
- **True and false worship both removed:** Keil & Delitzsch say items from both appear because Israel had mixed them. God would take away both kinds of worship, along with self-government. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/hosea-3.html
- **Wesley:** No king from their own royal line, foreign governors over them, no lawful sacrifice. Teraphim were household idols. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/
- **Matthew Henry:** no priesthood, no oracle, all in the dark. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Hsa/Hsa_003.cfm
- **Without idols too:** Precept Austin highlights that Israel would lack sacrifice yet not return to idolatry. https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-3-commentary

**Where interpreters differ**
- **What are the teraphim?** Barnes says they were idolatrous tools for divination. Matthew Henry notes some think they meant the Urim and Thummim. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/3-4.html; https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Hsa/Hsa_003.cfm
- **When is it fulfilled?**
  - *Exile:* Wesley applies it to the captivity. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/
  - *Gap between the Testaments:* Coffman applies it to the period between the Old and New Testaments. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/hosea-3.html
  - *Jews' present dispersion:* Gill, Clarke and Gaebelein apply it to the dispersion since the Temple fell. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/3.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/hosea-3.html
  - *Doesn't matter:* The Pulpit homiletics says the choice is immaterial. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/hosea/3.htm

## v. 5

**Traditional reading**
- **"David their king" is the Messiah:** Wesley, Ellicott, Benson, Barnes and Gill all say so, noting that the Targum and older Jewish interpreters read it the same way. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-5.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/3-5.html
- **Calvin (Reformed):** The return is the fruit of God's discipline, and naming the true God sets him against all the Baals. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/hosea-3.html
- **Trembling at his goodness:** Gill says it is a reverent, childlike fear, not slavish fear. Precept Austin says the trembling comes from God's goodness, not his anger. https://studylight.org/commentaries/geb/hosea-3.html; https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-3-commentary

**Where traditions differ: what are "the last days"?**
- **The gospel age, now:**
  - *Wesley (Methodist):* In the days of the Messiah, in gospel - times. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-hosea/
  - *Coffman:* the "new Israel" is in view. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/hosea/3-5.html
- **A future turning of the Jewish people to Jesus:**
  - *Gill (Baptist):* Israel will repent of unbelief and trust Christ. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/3.htm
  - *Pulpit homiletics:* Israel will one day accept Jesus as David's heir. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/hosea/3.htm
- **A future millennial kingdom (Christ's thousand-year reign):**
  - *Guzik:* the ultimate fulfilment is in the millennial kingdom, though anyone can know restoration now by turning back to God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-3/
  - *Gaebelein and Kingcomments:* the "afterward" is still future and points to Christ's return and reign. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/hosea-3.html; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kng/hosea-3.html
- **Leaves the time open:** Ellicott says the phrase means the distant future and is fulfilled only in the Messiah's reign. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/hosea/3-5.htm

**Jewish readings (as reported by Christian commentators)**
- The Pulpit Commentary reports that Rashi read "afterward" as after the Captivity, and Kimchi as near the time of salvation. https://biblehub.com/hosea/3-5.htm
